newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, US aim for ministers' insurance talks Dec 6.
newsitem.headline: Japan, US aim for ministers' insurance talks Dec 6.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Tuesday that Japan and the United States aim to hold a meeting between him and U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky on a bilateral insurance dispute on December 6 in Tokyo.
Senior officials from Japan and the United States have been holding a two-day meeting in Tokyo, scheduled to end on Tuesday, on opening up Japan's insurance market.
Japanese and U.S. negotiators remain apart on how to open the market, Mitsuzuka told a regular news conference.
"Japan and the United States are now working to arrange for a ministerial meeting on the insurance issue, to be held in Tokyo on December 6," he said.
Mitsuzuka said Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto had instructed him to reach an agreement on the issue by an agreed deadline of December 15.
"There are no issues that cannot be solved if we wish to do so," Mitsuzuka said.
Japan and the United States are at odds over implementation of a 1994 bilateral agreement to open Japan's $382 billion insurance market.

Washington had accused Tokyo of reneging on the agreement by moving to deregulate its "third sector" niche insurance market -- for such cover as personal accident and health care insurance -- in which foreign firms have a strong foothold, before opening its primary life and casualty markets.
The two nations originally set a July 31 deadline to settle the dispute, but agreed in October to push back the deadline to December 15.
